closed_forms.the beach face slope: the Dean profile d = A y^(2/3) has dd/dy = (2/3) A y^(-1/3), which diverges at the shoreline because uniform dissipation per unit water VOLUME has no water volume there. The face is the tangent at the handover depth: y_0 = (d/A)^(3/2), tan(beta) = (2/3) A^(3/2)/sqrt(d) = 0.052819. Checked against a finite difference on `dean_bed`, written in wave 1 for the submarine bed, and against the evolved 1-D loop's own slope (0.052947, 0.24%).
closed_forms.the swash excursion: R = xi H with xi = tan(beta)/sqrt(H/L_0) is R = tan(beta) sqrt(H L_0), so the HORIZONTAL reach R/tan(beta) = sqrt(H L_0) and the slope cancels identically. 13.7708 m at the swell, 19.4748 m at the file's own storm. The width of a dry beach with no constant in it.
closed_forms.the wet/dry boundary: run-up heights inherit the incident waves' Rayleigh statistics, so the wetted share is the exceedance exp(-(z/R)^2): 1 at the waterline, 0.368 at the run-up limit, 0.018 at twice it, with the median at z = R sqrt(ln 2) = 0.6056 m. Checked against 400000 Rayleigh variates from a generator that has never heard of beaches. Nothing is placed and no width is chosen.
closed_forms.the wet albedo split: a_wet = R_EXT + (1-R_EXT)(1-R_INT) a/(1 - a R_INT). The leading R_EXT is light that never entered the film -- the SPECULAR reflection off its surface -- so the diffuse lobe gets a_wet - R_EXT and the specular lobe gets fresnel(theta_v). R_EXT is the hemispherical average, which is the right thing to REMOVE from an albedo lit by a hemisphere; fresnel(theta_v) is the directional form, which is the right thing to ADD as a lobe. Same physics, two integrals.
closed_forms.the extinction coefficient: beta = tau/H over an exponential atmosphere of scale height H. atmosphere.TAU_R is the zenith optical depth derived four waves ago for the sun's own colour, so the Rayleigh half needs NO new constant: 1.1878e-05 /m in green. Koschmieder's beta = -ln(0.02)/V supplies the aerosol half and is the wave's one new `?`.
closed_forms.the airlight: in a horizontally homogeneous atmosphere a horizontal path of INFINITE length reaches exactly the radiance of the sky at the horizon in that azimuth -- that is what the horizon sky IS. So the airlight is sky_radiance on the ray flattened to the horizontal: no new number, the right azimuthal structure, and the sea-sky seam closes identically at grazing whatever beta and whatever the colour are.
closed_forms.the shadow reach: nothing casts a shadow further than its height over the tangent of the sun's elevation, so the march stops at h_max/tan(el) -- 42 m at 21 deg and 12 m at 56 deg, against wave 7's fixed 600 m for the same answer.

HUNT'S RUN-UP CANNOT PRODUCE A BERM CREST, AND THIS CONTRADICTS THE ORDINARY PICTURE OF A BEACH. A berm crest is a BREAK IN SLOPE and needs the swell to CUT the storm-built profile, which is swash transport this model does not have. What this bed carries is a face, a marked berm LEVEL and a flat backshore; the scarp is `?` and ABSENT, not approximated. Equilibrium is Q = 0, CERC is Q proportional to sin(2 theta_loc), so equilibrium is theta_loc = 0; Snell is sin(theta_b) = (c_b/c_0) sin(theta_0,local) and c_b/c_0 is never zero, so theta_b = 0 requires theta_0,local = 0 at EVERY station; integrating phi_s = -theta_0 gives x_s = x_ref - tan(theta_0)(y - y_mid), ONE STRAIGHT LINE rotated to face the swell, and ANY curvature raises the transport. terrain-architect chapter 12's clause 'headlands retreat faster than bays ... until the coast STRAIGHTENS' is therefore a THEOREM for the wave field that chapter assumes -- and exactly why it cannot produce the commonest sandy-coast plan-form there is. A bay is a property of a shoreline AND the headland that shelters it; it exists only where the orthogonal FANS, and the fan is diffraction, which no ray model has. MEASURED, four shorelines, one spectrum, one ramp, one transform, one closure, one array different: straight 9.233e-02 m3/s at 6.469 deg; the closed-form zero-transport coast 5.127e-03 at 0.202 deg; the BAY under a plane crest 1.875e-01 at 5.595 deg, TWICE THE STRAIGHT COAST; the bay under the fan its own pole implies 7.921e-02, and 2.650e-02 over the spiral span, 3.5x below straight. HONEST ANSWER TO THE BAR: NOT ZERO. 2.65e-02 against a MEASURED floor of 1.78e-03, about 15x the floor -- small, and attributable rather than absorbed: 0.71 deg is the ramp not being concentric with the curve it is keyed to (contours that are x-translates of a CONCAVE shoreline CONVERGE, and rebuilding the same circular bay with the depth a function of distance from the pole removes exactly that much) and 1.46 deg is the column march meeting curvature (the same march on straight contours at the same 20 deg leaves 0.20 deg). THE GEOMETRY: the log spiral is DERIVED and not fitted -- a constant residual obliquity forces a constant tangent-to-radius angle, and that is the logarithmic spiral and nothing else -- with the CIRCLE (alpha = 90 deg, shore normal to a radial orthogonal) the one member derivable end to end. The pole solves TWO conditions to 5e-14 and has no freedom left, so the indentation 122.79 m over 1409 m is an OUTPUT; it is 2.46x bar J's ~50 m and STAYS 2.46x. The inversion -- what deep-water obliquity WOULD give 50 m over 1408 m -- is 8.45 deg against the declared 20, a measurement of the offshore spectrum out of a plan-form and a calibration refused.

closed_forms.the zero-transport plan-form: Q proportional to sin(2 theta_loc) and Snell sin(theta_b) = (c_b/c_0) sin(theta_0,loc) give theta_b = 0 <=> theta_0,loc = 0 <=> phi_s = -theta_0, so x_s(y) = x_ref - tan(theta_0)(y - y_mid). THE ANGLE IS THE DEEP-WATER ONE. Rotating by the BREAKING angle instead (6.56 deg against 20) leaves 2.78 deg and 43 per cent of the transport; this file shipped that version first and the suite caught it.
closed_forms.why the logarithmic spiral: if the orthogonals radiate from a pole, shore normal to the orthogonal reads shore normal to the RADIUS and the curve is a circular arc about the pole EXACTLY (alpha = 90 deg). If the orthogonal is rotated off the radius by a CONSTANT delta, the tangent makes the constant angle 90 - delta with the radius at every station, and a constant tangent-to-radius angle is the logarithmic spiral's own definition and nothing else's. dP/dphi = R(cot(a) u + u_perp), whose angle to u is atan(tan a) = a, independent of phi. So the spiral is THE curve of constant residual obliquity and the empirical fit is what its ONE parameter absorbs.
closed_forms.the pole, closed with no freedom left: a log spiral has four freedoms; two anchors absorb R_a and phi_a and leave the similarity condition ln(r2/r1) = cot(alpha)(phi2 - phi1), one equation. Hsu & Evans' downcoast control point -- where the beach becomes parallel to the incoming crests -- gives tangent(A2) . khat = 0. Two equations, two unknowns, damped Newton to 5e-14. The downcoast tangent's bearing is then recomputed from the SAMPLED shoreline and comes back at exactly -theta_0, which is a check rather than a restatement.
closed_forms.the fan a shoreline requires: theta_loc = 0 demands the orthogonal lie at -phi_s(y); its alongshore RANGE is the swing the sheltering headland must supply. Pure geometry, no wave model in it. 39.6 deg on this bay.
closed_forms.the offshore Snell invariant: the conserved wavenumber component is the one along the CONTOUR, not along the grid's alongshore axis. The two agree only for a coast whose contours are the grid's rows.

overturned: WAVE 8 SAID THIS BED HAS 50 m OF PLAN CURVATURE. It has 52-55 m of shoreline RANGE and that is not the same claim. Fit a line to the coastal loop's shoreline and the residual is roughness at the hardness field's 380 m correlation length -- jagged, alternating seaward and landward every two or three rows, with no single curve in it. The bay-scale component is a few metres. Two claims, one number, and only the first was ever measured; _sec_embay now carries the separation as a row.

transform_2d's OFFSHORE BOUNDARY WAS WRONG FOR ANY COAST BUT A STRAIGHT ONE, AND EIGHT WAVES SHIPPED IT. It conserved k_y on the GRID's alongshore axis; the Snell invariant is the component along the CONTOUR. Nothing could see it because every scene in this project had grid-parallel contours until a shore curved. Found by CALIBRATING THE METER rather than by looking for it: the closed-form zero-transport coast must break at exactly theta = 0, and the old boundary left 4.89 deg of residual obliquity and 76 per cent of the straight coast's transport. With contour0 it leaves 0.2015 deg. A twenty-fourfold error, invisible to every row in the file, exposed by adding a control whose answer was known in advance.

WAVE 8's PREDICTION THAT GAP 4 (the eye height) IS 'COUPLED TO #1 AND NOT FIXABLE WITHOUT IT' IS FALSIFIED, AND IN THE DIRECTION THE ARGUMENT DID NOT ALLOW FOR. The bay moved the shoreline, not the cliff brow: on the embayed bed the brow the camera stands on reads 15.71 m against wave 8's 17.31, so it went the WRONG WAY -- the bay's landward limb pushes the shoreline inland and the cliff foot with it. Closing gap 1 made gap 4 slightly worse.

THE FIRST POLE SOLVE WENT TO THE WRONG BRANCH AND LOOKED PLAUSIBLE. A pole at infinity is always a root -- a spiral with an infinitely distant pole is a straight line -- so Newton from a naive start returned D at 79 km, a residual of 5e-03 it had not converged to, and an indentation of 1.37 m. The rule is now explicit and physical (the pole is the sheltering headland's diffraction point; a pole 79 km offshore is not a headland) and both branches are reported.

THE PROJECT'S OWN 'THE BAY MAKES THE REFRACTION CHECKABLE' IS TRUE, AND ITS COROLLARY IS NOT WHAT WAVE 8 EXPECTED. The bay does NOT reduce the transport under the wave field the file computes -- it DOUBLES it. Building bar J's subject made the scene's largest physics gap visible rather than closing it, and that gap is diffraction.
marked_open: DELTA, the residual obliquity that fixes alpha. Only delta = 0 (the circle) is derived. Bracketed rather than asserted: the circle's indentation is 121.68 m against the spiral's 122.79, 0.9 per cent, so the `?` is worth less than the two anchors are. Silvester's published alpha for real bays is 30-50 deg, i.e. delta = 40-60, an order above anything refraction leaves -- an EMPIRICAL fit to a different quantity and it must not be confused with this one.

HSU & EVANS' PARABOLIC BAY-SHAPE EQUATION, NAMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED. Fifteen fitted quartic coefficients with no internal consistency check that would catch a wrong digit, and nothing in this container holds the paper. Writing them from memory would manufacture a citation. Its advantage over the spiral is precisely that it produces the straight downcoast tangent inside one formula instead of as a join.

THE FAN IS A BOUNDARY CONDITION AND NOT A DIFFRACTION SOLVE. The 39.6 deg the bay needs is supplied as a stated per-row offshore direction radiating from the bay's own pole. A Sommerfeld / Penney-Price edge stamped at the headland tip would make it an OUTPUT. This is now the largest unbuilt piece of water physics in the project and it is the same term chapter 12's diffraction section prices for the isolated-rock case.

THE RAMP IS KEYED CROSS-SHORE, NOT CONCENTRICALLY, and it is worth 0.71 deg of residual obliquity. Measured with `plan_ramp_polar` rather than argued. A two-line change with a large blast radius (bay_bed's whole composition), named and priced and not taken.

THE COLUMN MARCH ON A CURVED BED, 1.46 deg. transform_2d carries the ray's alongshore drift only through its dk/dy terms; at 20 deg the drift is 0.36 of a cell per step against the 0.015 the function's own comment quotes for the near-normal case.

THE INDENTATION IS 2.46x THE PHOTOGRAPH'S AND STAYS THAT WAY. The standing ruling forbids calibrating on the photographs, so it is reported. The inversion is the finding: the deep-water obliquity that WOULD give 50 m over 1408 m is 8.45 deg against the file's declared 20, which is a measurement of the offshore spectrum out of a plan-form.
